One S1/T1 case: vertical, relaxed and adiabatic energies, and both DeltaE_ST.

    python run_state_pair.py --system formaldehyde --reference HF         --out results/state_pairs.jsonl

DeltaE_ST has two conventions that are not small perturbations of one another:

    vertical    Omega_S1(R0) - Omega_T1(R0), both states at the ground minimum
    adiabatic   [E_S1(R_S1) - E_0(R0)] - [E_T1(R_T1) - E_0(R0)], each state at
                its own minimum

They differ by exactly the difference of the two relaxation energies, which is
why both are reported together with that identity as a residual: where
lambda_S1 and lambda_T1 disagree, a vertical DeltaE_ST is not the barrier that
governs up-conversion.

Triplets use kappa = KAPPA['triplet'] = 0 in the bare-exchange term. The dense
qb route carries them too -- `BSEqb` takes `spin` and sets kappa from it -- so
`run_dense_state_pair.py` is an interpolation-free reference for these, not
only for singlets; the claim that it refuses triplets is stale. Range-separated
hybrids give correct energies but their skeleton derivative is refused, so pair
them with --no-gradients.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --system SYSTEM       molecule: a name resolved in --geom-dir (H2O, a4,
                        chl_dimer), an explicit .xyz path, or 'aN' for a
                        generated acene when the test set has no file for it.
  --target {bse-gw,bse,qp,rpa}
                        which gradient. 'bse-gw' is production: a BSE
                        excitation energy on a quasiparticle diagonal, so the
                        reverse pass runs the BSE adjoint, the QP set adjoint
                        and the screening adjoint. 'bse' puts mean-field
                        energies on the diagonal and skips the QP chain
                        entirely -- the difference between the two rows is
                        what the GW layer costs on a gradient. 'qp' is one
                        quasiparticle energy, no BSE at all. 'rpa' is the dRPA
                        correlation energy of the ground state: the imaginary-
                        frequency integral of Tr[ln(1 - chi0) + chi0] on the
                        same proj(tau), so its reverse pass is one
                        polarizability sweep and nothing else -- the floor
                        every other target sits on. The value is E_c (not the
                        total energy) and the gradient is dE_c/dR; add the
                        mean field's own gradient for a force.
  --state STATE         BSE root index (0 = lowest) for the bse targets; for
                        --target qp, an ORBITAL index offset from the HOMO, so
                        0 is the HOMO and +1 the LUMO.
  --spin {singlet,triplet}
  --tda                 Tamm-Dancoff. Note this is not only an approximation
                        knob: a triplet on a reference with min eig(A-B) < 0
                        has no real full-BSE root at all, and `bse_solve`
                        raises rather than returning a complex energy.
  --solver {auto,dense,davidson}
                        Casida solver. 'dense' builds the (n_ov, n_ov) blocks
                        and diagonalizes -- the reference, and the only route
                        a finite-difference check should use, since it returns
                        every root in a fixed order. It is also impossible at
                        size: n_ov ~ 6.9e4 at a10/cc-pVDZ is 38 GB per block
                        and an O(n_ov^3) eigensolve. `davidson` is matrix-free
                        through `solve_bse_isdf` and never forms a block.
                        'auto' picks dense below --dense-max-nov and davidson
                        above. The ADJOINT is matrix-free either way --
                        `bse_cache` gives `bse_backward` exactly the three-
                        index blocks it needs, so the solver choice never
                        reaches it.
  --dense-max-nov DENSE_MAX_NOV
                        n_ov ceiling for --solver auto. 12000 is ~1.2 GB per
                        block and a few minutes of eigh.
  --nroots NROOTS       roots for the Davidson route; must exceed --state.
  --bse-conv-tol BSE_CONV_TOL
                        Davidson residual tolerance, tighter than the solver's
                        own 1e-5 default because Hellmann-Feynman reads the
                        EIGENVECTORS and their convergence lands in the force
                        directly. THAT REASONING IS THE PRECAUTION, NOT A
                        MEASURED EFFECT: swept on water/cc-pVDZ the gradient
                        moves 1.7e-08, 1.5e-08, 1.8e-08, 7.4e-09 Ha/Bohr from
                        the dense route at 1e-5, 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-10 -- a
                        plateau, not a convergence, and the same size as each
                        route's own residual against finite differences (dense
                        1.5e-07, Davidson 1.3e-07 relative, on the same DF
                        mean field). So the two solvers agree to within the
                        floor, the floor is not the eigensolver, and this knob
                        buys nothing measurable at that size. It is kept tight
                        because the plateau has only been mapped there; relax
                        it if the Davidson iteration count becomes the cost.
  --basis BASIS
  --auxbasis AUXBASIS   default <basis>-ri. THE AUXILIARY BASIS CONTROLS THE
                        ENERGY and the grid controls the GRADIENT -- they are
                        separate error channels and tightening the wrong one
                        buys nothing. Measured on the reference systems, cc-
                        pvtz-ri with --counts 14,9,5,2 lands 4 meV / 0.07%
                        from the dense reference.
  --counts A1,A2,A3,B1  radial shells per Lebedev sub-shell; default 8,5,3,1 =
                        148 points/atom. This is the GRADIENT accuracy knob:
                        the gradient error follows grid density while the
                        energy error follows the auxiliary basis, so a
                        converged energy is no evidence at all about the
                        force. Raising it costs M^2 in the Gram.
  --n-start N_START     L-BFGS-B descents per element when optimizing the grid
                        radii. Cached per (element, basis, counts, n_start),
                        so it is a one-time offline cost; six descents cut a
                        benzene exchange error 23x at the same point count.
  --qp-window QP_WINDOW
                        quasiparticle orbitals as N occupied below the HOMO
                        and N virtual above the LUMO, so the default 2 is a
                        set of 4. 'all' puts every orbital on the set. The
                        orbitals OUTSIDE the set keep their mean-field
                        energies on the BSE diagonal; that is a physical
                        approximation, it is recorded in the output, and it is
                        frozen across a stencil like everything else here.
  --degeneracy-tol DEGENERACY_TOL
                        Hartree. Orbitals closer than this are treated as one
                        degenerate block and the quasiparticle window is
                        widened outward to contain whole blocks. A SPLIT
                        DEGENERATE PAIR IS A FIFTH DISCONTINUITY, and it is
                        the one a window silently creates. Inside a degenerate
                        subspace the individual eigenvectors are not
                        determined, so "orbital 3" is not a smooth function of
                        the geometry: one half of the pair gets a
                        quasiparticle energy, the other keeps the mean field,
                        and a symmetry-breaking displacement rotates which is
                        which. Ammonia/cc-pVDZ splits TWO pairs at the default
                        window -- the 1e pair at 2.3e-05 Ha and the 2e
                        virtuals at 2.7e-06 -- and the BSE@GW gradient then
                        misses finite differences by 1.3e-01 relative,
                        entirely in the components that break C3. The z
                        components, which preserve it, are correct to 1e-08 in
                        the same run. The diagnosis is sharp because the
                        neighbouring targets are clean: --target qp reads ONE
                        nondegenerate orbital and lands 1.8e-08, --target bse
                        uses no window at all and lands 3.1e-07. Only the
                        combination fails, which is what points at the window
                        rather than at either chain.
  --ntau-gw NTAU_GW     imaginary-time points for the GW self-energy.
  --ntau-w NTAU_W       imaginary-time points for the static screening; 'auto'
                        takes `minimax_points_for_bse`.
  --ntau-rpa NTAU_RPA   imaginary-time points for --target rpa; 'auto' takes
                        `minimax_points_for_accuracy` on the reference range.
  --nfreq-rpa NFREQ_RPA
                        Gauss-Legendre points on the imaginary-frequency
                        integral of E_c for --target rpa; default
                        RPA_ENERGY_NFREQ.
  --nfreq-cd NFREQ_CD   Gauss-Legendre points on the contour-deformation
                        integral; default CD_NFREQ, and the chain doubles it
                        from there while its first frequency does not resolve
                        the distance from a quasiparticle root to the nearest
                        pole of G. The route is CD rather than an analytic
                        continuation because Pade is not differentiable: its
                        coefficients come from a solve whose conditioning is
                        the whole point, and the derivative of the continued
                        function is not the continuation of the derivative.
  --e-min-below-gap E_MIN_BELOW_GAP
                        lower the GW tau grid this far BELOW the gap, in
                        Hartree, so the Laplace residue backend can still
                        carry a residue frequency. Default: half the gap,
                        which is a ratio and therefore transfers between
                        molecules. A FIXED shift does not -- 0.5 Ha is a third
                        of the gap on water/cc-pVDZ and larger than the whole
                        gap on naphthalene, where it drove e_min into the 1e-3
                        floor, took e_max/e_min to 1.5e4, and the minimax
                        transform fit to 2.5e-01. That grid still ran; it was
                        a warning, not an error.
  --residue-route {auto,explicit,laplace,none,sop}
                        how W at a REAL frequency is built for states whose
                        root has crossed a neighbouring orbital energy. Cubic
                        is 'laplace' (cos -> cosh out of proj(tau)), which
                        needs the tau grid to reach down to gap - w';
                        'explicit' goes through C_ov = B[:, occ, virt] and is
                        the O(N^4) end of the route. 'sop' has no residues at
                        all: W is modelled by auxiliary poles so the self-
                        energy is closed form in omega, and a state Eq. (27)
                        does not admit falls back to 'auto'. the route.
                        DEFAULT 'explicit', NOT 'auto', and the reason is a
                        real failure rather than caution. `residue_route_auto`
                        reads the residue set at the Newton START; a frontier
                        state has none there and is given no backend at all,
                        and then the quasiparticle shift moves its root ACROSS
                        a neighbour and the iteration meets a residue it was
                        told it would not. On naphthalene/cc-pVDZ that is not
                        an edge case: the HOMO and LUMO both take that branch
                        and the run dies inside the forward solve. The margin
                        that guards the other states (RESIDUE_FREQ_MARGIN)
                        does not apply to an EMPTY set. It is also close to
                        free at any useful window: the states one in from the
                        frontier have residues ABOVE the gap -- measured on
                        naphthalene at every e_min from 1e-3 to the full gap
                        -- so C_ov is built for them whatever this is set to,
                        and reusing it for the frontier pair adds a wrapper.
                        Set it to auto only with --qp-window 0, and expect the
                        failure above.
  --sop-poles SOP_POLES
                        auxiliary poles M for --residue-route sop. The default
                        is set by the GRADIENT rather than the energy, which
                        converges at fewer; this flag is what shows that.
  --sop-stride SOP_STRIDE
                        fit the common poles on every n-th orbital column.
                        Placement moves dSigma/domega more than Sigma, so a
                        stride that is harmless for an energy need not be for
                        a force.
  --scissor SCISSOR     frozen quasiparticle shift, Ha, for the states the
                        pole model cannot carry (reach >= 1). Without it those
                        states fall back to the real-axis residue route.
                        Calibrate it at the REFERENCE geometry. 'calibrate'
                        does that automatically: the excluded states are
                        solved there by the fallback route and their roots
                        become the frozen shifts. A FIXED number is the crude
                        alternative and costs up to 7.5 meV and 3e-4 Ha/Bohr
                        at zero.
  --tile-gb TILE_GB     working-set cap on the tiled (M, M) intermediates in
                        the BSE adjoint; the module default is used when
                        unset.
  --frames {frozen,continued}
                        how the atom-local Lebedev shells are ORIENTED as the
                        nuclei move. The interpolation points are r_g = p_g
                        F_i + R_i, and F_i is the covariant frame of
                        `atomic_frames` -- the eigenvectors of that atom's
                        weighted direction tensor. 'continued' recomputes F_i
                        at each geometry and matches each axis to the
                        reference. It is what the small-molecule gates use and
                        it is exact where the tensor is nondegenerate.
                        'frozen' keeps the reference frames at every geometry,
                        so the points translate with their atom and never
                        turn, and the matching `with_frames=False` adjoint is
                        then the exact derivative of that function. FROZEN IS
                        THE DEFAULT BECAUSE A DEGENERATE DIRECTION TENSOR IS
                        COMMON AND NOT FLAGGED. Ammonia's nitrogen has
                        eigenvalues 0.67384 / 0.67378 / 0.23429 -- a relative
                        gap of 8.1e-05 that `atomic_frames` does not mark
                        degenerate -- and the eigenvector adjoint's
                        1/(lambda_a - lambda_b) then amplifies a 0.19% branch
                        by ~1e4. Continued frames on NH3/cc-pVDZ miss finite
                        differences by 17x the gradient itself, on EVERY
                        target including the bare quasiparticle one; frozen
                        frames land at 1e-7. Water is unaffected either way
                        (its smallest gap is 0.40), which is why the gates
                        never saw this. Nothing is given up. The frame is a
                        gauge on a numerical grid, not a physical object: the
                        energy is invariant to it to 1.4e-14, so freezing it
                        removes a dependence the answer does not have. It is
                        only over a LARGE displacement that a frozen frame
                        fits worse, and a gradient is taken at a point.
  --scf-auxbasis SCF_AUXBASIS

                        df. Default None = pyscf's own JK-fitting set. This is

                        correlation/ISDF one: a -ri set fits J/K badly and
                        silently biases every quantity downstream.
  --scf {df,direct}     'df' density-fits the mean field, which is what makes
                        a real system reachable at all. It is NOT free on the
                        gradient side: pyscf's conventional and density-fitted
                        derivative J/K do not share a convention, and the
                        fitted skeleton is built from the three- and two-
                        centre adjoints directly (`fock_partial_skeleton_df`)
                        rather than through the conventional weights, which
                        were wrong by 8.4e-03 on a gradient of 5.74.
  --xc XC               exchange-correlation functional of a Kohn-Sham
                        reference (pyscf name, e.g. pbe0); default is Hartree-
                        Fock. On a Kohn-Sham reference the chain carries the
                        static <Sigma_x - v_xc> term and its two derivative
                        pieces itself, weighted by the pole strength.
  --environment ENVIRONMENT
                        surroundings: 'none' for the gas phase, 'water' or any
                        other name in pyscf's SMD table, or 'EPS:EPS_STATIC'
                        for an explicit pair of dielectric constants. The
                        optical one screens the response and the static one
                        relaxes the ground state (Duchemin, Guido, Jacquemin
                        and Blase, Chem. Sci. 9, 4430 (2018)); a name supplies
                        both. The chain owns both halves, so the SCF this
                        runner hands it is re-converged inside PCM(eps_static)
                        before anything reads it, and every row of a solvated
                        case carries the constants it ran at.
  --threads THREADS
  --max-memory MAX_MEMORY
                        pyscf max_memory in MB.
  --fd FD               finite-difference spot check: 'none', 'all' (every
                        coordinate -- only for small systems), or "ia,x" for
                        one component. Each component costs FOUR full energy
                        builds on the 5-point stencil, so "0,2" on a real
                        system is a validation you can afford and --fd all is
                        not. The check redoes the SCF, the factors, the QP
                        solve, the screening and the Casida solve at each
                        displacement -- nothing is held fixed except the four
                        frozen conventions above, which is the whole point.
  --fd-h FD_H           displacement in BOHR; 5-point stencil (-2h,-h,+h,+2h).

                        defect in the gradient is INDEPENDENT of h, and
                        stencil truncation falls as h^4. Only reference noise
                        rises as h shrinks.

Score a grid by the observable, not by the fit error.

The fit error is what the radii search minimizes, and it is a poor judge of the
grid: this repo has it improving 167x while the exchange error got WORSE, and
anti-correlated with |dE_x| on carbon's own candidates. So a box chosen on fit
error alone is not chosen. This scores a candidate grid on BSE@G0W0 excitation
energies against the DF route at the same geometry and mean field, which is the
quantity the grid exists to reproduce.

    python score_grids_gwbse.py --molecule pyridine --basis aug-cc-pvdz         --counts 8,5,3,1 --r-max 5 12 --table sweep_radii.json

Each row is one (molecule, basis, counts, r_max) against the DF reference, in
meV per state. Rows append to a JSONL and a rerun skips what is already there,
so this resumes after a wall clock.

The reference is `solve_bse_df` at the SAME mean field, so the comparison
isolates the grid: both routes see one set of orbitals and differ only in how
the two-electron integrals are factorized. Judging an ISDF root against a DF
root from a separately converged SCF would fold the SCF difference in, and at
148 points that is the larger of the two.

Vertical only, and that is HALF the target: the grids are judged on vertical
AND adiabatic excitation energies. An adiabatic energy is a difference between
two relaxed geometries, so it depends on the excited-state FORCE, and a grid
error that is small at one geometry can still slope with the nuclei -- on
benzene's breathing mode the signed S1 error runs -50.7 meV/A on one grid and
+24.8 meV/A on another, opposite in sign, which no single-geometry check sees.
The adiabatic arm is available: `radii` is a SHARED setting on `RPABSESurface`
and reaches `_one_factorization`, so both chains see one grid.
